problem: Prior scene representations either abstract observations too early (scene graphs like ConceptGraph lose visual evidence) or keep flat image sets (3D-Mem) without structure. They also do not tell the agent what level of additional information is missing, so exploration scope is not adapted.
motivation: Embodied agents facing changing tasks need a task-agnostic memory that keeps rich visual evidence but supports flexible, budgeted access. The observation is that the abstraction level at which retrieval finds relevant cues (room, view, object) indicates how missing information can be gathered, so exploration options can be structured by the retrieval outcome.
key_idea: Build a task-agnostic room-view-object hierarchy of actual observations, retrieve coarse-to-fine with an LLM, and let the retrieved level activate matching exploration options (room exploration, view refinement, frontier).
insight: Ablations on EM-EQA show every layer helps, and replacing the co-visibility-based view selection with 3D-Mem's selection causes the largest drop (63.5 to 54.2) despite using fewest frames, so view selection preserving diverse co-visibility is the key. On A-EQA, removing room exploration or view refinement lowers both accuracy and SPL, showing multi-scale exploration options help. Hierarchical retrieval also reduces lexical exact-match errors and the number of images queried to the VLM.
method: Object layer: ConceptGraph-style object update; each node is the best object-centric crop; a visibility mask M links objects to views.

View layer: agglomerative clustering of objects by child-aware co-visibility similarity; representative views are assigned in inverse merge order by CLIP dissimilarity, redundant clusters are pruned; updated incrementally.
Room layer: GPT-4o-mini predicts room types and object-room probabilities per view, accumulated by Bayesian update; room-view links are fused from direct predictions and object cues.

Hierarchical retrieval: one LLM query per layer selects up to k=5 nodes, restricting the next layer to connected nodes; at view level the LLM picks relevant classes then views are greedily selected to cover them.

Exploration options: room exploration (clusters of unexplored area with target positions projected onto views and an occupancy map), view refinement (closer/wider/different angle, using SAM3 masks), and frontier exploration (default, as in 3D-Mem, with anti-oscillation matching).
VLM selects only a high-level option; target coordinates are precomputed; a separate VLM termination check decides sufficiency of the retrieved information.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (2024-11-20, frozen) for retrieval, exploration selection, termination and answering; GPT-4o-mini for room layer; SAM3 and CLIP as components
setting.action_space: high-level target positions (room clusters, frontiers, refined viewpoints) executed by Habitat-Sim pathfinder
setting.privileged: collision-free path planner assumed (Habitat built-in pathfinder); no GT map

numbers_note: OpenEQA is not in the canonical bench list with EM/A-EQA split; entries use 'OpenEQA' with split 'val' as no official split names are given. Ablation results (300-episode EM-EQA subset: 63.5 full) are not listed as separate entries.
results: Ours reaches 61.5 LLM-Match on EM-EQA (vs 57.2 for 3D-Mem), 54.5 LLM-Match / 45.0 SPL on A-EQA (vs re-run 3D-Mem 49.6 / 37.0), and 72.7 SR / 51.5 SPL on GOAT-Bench (vs 3D-Mem 69.1 / 48.9). It also queries fewer images during exploration (2.34 vs 3.26).
limitations: Relies on VLM/LLM reasoning, which is sensitive to perception and language errors
Assumes a collision-free planner (Habitat pathfinder) and evaluates only in simulation on subsets
Static environments and limited horizon; dynamic scenes and longer-horizon tasks are left for future work
